trap-negation-contrast.evidence: 'The nuclear chart is not a phenomenological fit; it is the set of integer solutions to an algebraic equation determined by the single parameter $q$.' - assert-by-denial in the diagnostic form, and the denial is doing the rhetorical work rather than drawing a mathematical distinction. It is also not the substantive-contrast false-positive class, because the block's own algebra contradicts the positive half: the curve depends on $c$, given three paragraphs later as $c = (q - q^{-1})\lambda_C/(2a_A)$, i.e. on $\lambda_C$ and $a_A$ as well as $q$ - and $a_A, a_C$ are the semi-empirical mass-formula coefficients, which ARE phenomenological fits.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: Structural - the construction cannot be removed without also settling the over-claim it carries, so not fixed inline. Proposed: state the positive claim at its true strength, e.g. 'The nuclear chart is the set of integer solutions to an algebraic equation whose single curvature parameter $c$ is fixed by $q$ together with the binding coefficients $\lambda_C$ and $a_A$.' Then say explicitly whether $\lambda_C$ and $a_A$ are derived or are inputs beyond CAL-1/2/3 (per AGENTS 'any input outside CAL-1/2/3 is a fourth calibration').
